\section*{Resumen de orientacion}
This document converts the approved career strategy into CV-ready material.

\section*{Contenido completo depurado}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Contenido completo depurado}




\subsection{Purpose}




This document converts the approved career strategy into CV-ready material.




It includes:




\begin{itemize}
\item a base one-page CV structure;
\item role-specific CV variants;
\item reusable bullet banks;
\item project descriptions;
\item skills blocks;
\item education wording;
\item training/course wording;
\item language and work-authorization wording;
\item claims to avoid;
\item editing rules.
\end{itemize}




This is not the final designed PDF CV. It is the source text for producing one-page ATS-friendly resumes.




\medskip\hrule\medskip




\section{1. CV positioning rules}




\subsection{Core identity}




Use this as the main professional identity:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist
\end{mdcode}




Expanded version:




\begin{mdcode}
Bloque de codigo: text
Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, and Unity WebGL deployment.
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{Primary CV target families}




Use separate variants for:




\begin{enumerate}
\item Real-Time 3D / Unity Developer.
\item Technical Visualization / Digital Twin / Simulation Developer.
\item Unity WebGL / Interactive 3D Developer.
\item Unity Technical Artist.
\item Tools / Python Automation Developer.
\end{enumerate}




\subsection{Do not use one generic CV for every job}




The base CV should be adapted per role family. The same facts can be reorganized, but the claims must remain consistent.




\subsection{Critical claim discipline}




Do not claim:




\begin{itemize}
\item Senior Technical Artist.
\item EU work authorization now.
\item German residence now.
\item Portuguese passport already issued.
\item Unity certification if not obtained.
\item Rebelway / CG Cookie / Alive certification if no certificate exists.
\item Production AI engineer.
\item Enterprise AI platform developer.
\item Commercially shipped Unity product unless true.
\item Full-stack specialist as primary identity.
\end{itemize}

\section{14. CV length and formatting rules}




\subsection{One-page target}




The default CV should be one page.




If needed, use a two-page technical resume only for:




\begin{itemize}
\item highly technical roles;
\item technical artist roles requiring detailed portfolio breakdown;
\item senior reviewers who explicitly ask for detail.
\end{itemize}

Header
Professional Summary
Technical Skills
Selected Projects
Experience
Education
Training
Languages / Availability
\end{mdcode}




\subsection{ATS formatting rules}




Use:




\begin{itemize}
\item plain section headers;
\item no icons;
\item no columns if ATS compatibility is critical;
\item simple bullets;
\item standard file name;
\item PDF for submission;
\item DOCX only if requested.

\section{16. Red-flag edits to avoid}




Do not:




\begin{itemize}
\item add too many unrelated technologies;
\item list every course;
\item list every repo;
\item exaggerate years of experience;
\item overemphasize full-stack;
\item overemphasize AI tooling;
\item overemphasize character art;
\item describe unfinished projects as complete;
\item hide the fact that TwinSight is academic;
\item make the CV read like a thesis abstract;
\item use dense paragraphs;
\item use vague phrases like “passionate,” “dynamic,” or “hardworking.”
\end{itemize}
